event: Daily Intelligence Briefing
title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Tech-led risk-off into a hawkish Fed.
September's flash PMIs (manufacturing 57.0 vs 53.6 fc, services 58.7 vs 56.0 fc) plus 4.6% 1-year inflation expectations locked in hike odds — CME FedWatch prices 100% for Oct 28 — and QQQ -1.07% with SOXX -2.08% paid the bill while defensives XLV +0.33% and XLP +0.27% held green.

INDICES — VIX 16.1, still 0.4 above its 15.7 20-day MA.
SOXX -2.08%, QQQ -1.07%, IJH -0.75%, SPY -0.74%, IWM -0.69%, DIA -0.67% — small beat large by just 0.07pp, a hollow win. Silver -5.49% and gold -3.94% were the loudest cross-asset breaks, real yields doing the damage.

VOLUME & BREADTH — SPY 1.0x and QQQ (losing group, SOXX 1.0x) show no capitulation volume, but IJH 2.0x and GLD 1.5x on down/flat tape read as distribution in mid-caps and metal liquidation. Breadth is the story: only 24% of S&P 500 names above the 50-DMA, 44% above the 200-DMA, adv/dec 163/334, up/down volume 0.41, and 87 new 60-day lows vs 11 highs — participation flatly contradicts the index-level calm. Narrow tape, no floor.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLV Health Care +0.33%, XLP Staples +0.27%, XLE Energy +0.10%, XLRE Real Estate -0.51%, XLU Utilities -0.66%, XLB Materials -0.66%, XLK Technology -0.89%, XLI Industrials -0.97%, XLF Financials -1.19%, XLY Discretionary -1.41%, XLC Comms -1.58%.
Top industries: USO +1.13%, XBI +1.02%. Bottom: SILJ -5.54%, SLV -5.49%, GDX -5.36%.
Five-day flows: XLY +$711mm (100th pct) and XLK +$147mm (60th) drew money while XLF bled -$2,305mm (0th pct) and XLV -$1,089mm (2nd) — financials are being dumped into weakness, a genuine exit. Money is hiding in healthcare staples and energy; it is leaving financials, comms and discretionary. Rotation state: defensive risk-off.

POSITIONING — SPY PCR 1.05 shows real hedging demand, QQQ PCR 0.75 does not; skew is positive across SPY +7.0% and QQQ +6.4%, so puts carry the premium. MOVE at 101.8 vs an 83.0 20-day MA is the loudest signal — bond vol is running 23% above trend and that is what is pressing equities.

CROSS-ASSET — Gold -3.94% and silver -5.49% falling alongside a rising dollar (UUP +0.28%) and 20-year yields (TLT -0.88%) is the classic real-rate transmission chain: hawkish repricing, not risk-off hedging, is driving metals. Next FOMC is Oct 28, with CME FedWatch at hold 0.0% / cut 0.0% / hike 100.0%; Polymarket separately prices 68% for a 25bp October hike, +4pp in five days.

SIGNALS & WATCH — Fear & Greed 52.9, Neutral.
QCOM -7.17%, BA -6.91% (2.8x vol, The Defense 7), INTC -5.67% led decliners; MDT +0.97% on 2.3x volume was the lone vol-spike gainer.
Watching: BA for whether 2.8x distribution volume follows through, IJH for its 2.0x mid-cap distribution signal, and GLD after -3.94% despite $1,112mm of five-day inflows — a flows-versus-price divergence worth resolving tomorrow.
